subject: Hosted API per-token commit & cross-region billing — Lighthouse AI
messages:
From: Emma Wallace <emma.wallace@lighthouseai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lighthouseai.com, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@lighthouseai.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 16:15:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood hosted API pricing — regional billing question

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our finance & procurement teams are trying to model cost for a 12-month rollout across our US and EU regions. A couple quick questions before we push this into our vendor shortlist:

1) Do your per-token usage discounts apply per-account globally, or are they calculated per-region (i.e., US tokens billed differently than EU/APAC)?
2) If we commit to a monthly spend tier (e.g., $40k/mo), can that commit be shared across regions, or does each region need a separate commitment?
3) Any standard language you use for currency exposure / FX if commits are in USD but invoicing is local?

We expect ~1.2B tokens/month in month 6 if we enable EU expansion — rough mix today is 70% US / 30% EU.

Would appreciate a short note that I can share with procurement.

Thanks,
Emma Wallace
Head of Product
Lighthouse AI
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Wallace <emma.wallace@lighthouseai.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing — regional billing question

Emma —

Thanks for the clear questions — appreciate the usage breakdown. Short answers up front, then a few options:

1) Global discounts: our usage-based discount schedule is tied to the customer account (one discount curve) not split by region; tokens consumed in any region count toward the same volume tiers. This lets customers aggregate usage across regions.

2) Commit flexibility: commits can be structured either as a single global commitment that covers multi-region usage (recommended), or as region-specific commits if you require separate SLAs/budgets per legal entity. The economic terms differ slightly; global commit yields better blended discounts.

3) Currency / invoicing: by default we invoice in USD. For local invoicing we offer a localized invoice option; we include an FX pass-through clause in the SOW or you can elect to take FX exposure on your side. We can surface both options on the SOW.

Attached is a short pricing matrix with example bands and two packaging options: (A) single global commit; (B) per-region commit. The matrix shows per-token effective price at different monthly token volumes and the delta when you enable EU as a second region.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix-APR2026.xlsx (pricing scenarios)

If helpful I can schedule 20 minutes with Aditya (our pricing/sales engineer) to walk through the math for your 70/30 split. If you send a baseline month-by-month forecast (tokens by region) we can produce a blended P&L for the first 12 months.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Emma Wallace <emma.wallace@lighthouseai.com>

Cc: procurement@lighthouseai.com
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 11:43:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing — regional billing question

Thanks Soojin — that helps. A few follow-ups from procurement:

• They want confirmation that discounts tier once per rolling 30-day window (monthly consumption) rather than calendar month — can you confirm?
• If we do a global commit, what happens if a sudden traffic spike is driven entirely by APAC (e.g., 90% of tokens in one region for a month) — do we lose the blended discount or is there an automatic fallback?
• What levers exist to limit cross-region burst costs (for example, routing lower-cost models to a cheaper region automatically)?

Procurement also asked for a sample SOW with invoicing terms and an initial 12-month mutual action plan. Can you send a draft SOW and a DocuSign-ready contract?

Emma

Subject: Fwd: Redwood hosted API pricing — Lighthouse AI procurement asks

Team — forwarding Lighthouse AI procurement questions. Key asks: rolling 30-day vs calendar month discounting, protection for APAC-driven spikes, levers to limit cross-region burst costs, and SOW + DocuSign.

Initial thinking:
- We confirm rolling 30-day usage windows for tiering — more favorable for customers with smoothing traffic.
- For APAC spikes: propose an automatic regional-cap fallback policy — when >X% of monthly spend occurs in a single region, we apply a temporary per-region cap rate for excess tokens above historical baseline; this preserves blended discount for the committed volume and charges incremental usage at a defined overage rate.
- Levers: routing by policy, model variant fallbacks (smaller/quantized model in region), and soft-cap alerts. Recommend including a clause in the SOW for a 30-day grace for region ramp-ups.

Action: Aditya, can you prepare a short pricing note that documents the math for a global $40k/mo commit with 70/30 US/EU mix, and an APAC spike scenario (90% APAC for one month) showing the effective blended per-token price + overage calculation? Priyom, confirm whether we can approve a one-time 10% cross-region uplift reduction for first 3 months as an incentive for Lighthouse to sign an annual commitment.

Thanks — Soojin

Subject: Pricing & SOW — Lighthouse AI (global commit options + APAC protection)

Emma / procurement team —

Great to align over the last few days. Per our conversations attached is: 1) a draft SOW (Lighthouse_AI_SOW_draft.pdf) with invoicing & FX options, 2) the redwood-pricing-matrix-APR2026.xlsx with worked examples for the $40k/mo global commit and the APAC-spike scenario, and 3) a summary of operational controls we recommend.

Highlights / proposal summary:
• Global commit: proposed $40,000/month USD for 12 months (Deal ID: DL-2026-0419-LHT). Tokens across US/EU/APAC count toward the same tier thresholds.
• Discounting window: rolling 30-day usage windows for tier calculations (not calendar month).
• APAC spike protection: for any 30-day window where a region exceeds 75% of that window's tokens, committed volume up to the agreed baseline preserves the blended commit pricing. Excess tokens above baseline are billed at a defined overage rate (see matrix). Additionally we can enable automated regional fallbacks to lower-precision model variants for burst mitigation.
• One-time incentive: approval to offer a 10% cross-region uplift discount for the first 3 months if Lighthouse signs a 12-month global commit within 14 days of this email. (This is a one-time concession documented in the SOW.)
• Invoicing: default USD invoices with optional local invoicing; FX clause available in SOW.

Next steps:
1) Review attached SOW and pricing matrix.
2) If acceptable, sign via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/abcdef123456 (link included)
3) Send month-by-month region forecast and we will finalize the exact blended per-token numbers and generate the signed schedule.

Attachments: Lighthouse_AI_SOW_draft.pdf, redwood-pricing-matrix-APR2026.xlsx

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
